target.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not currently have an official installable MXC sandbox backend for Windows hosts that can run sandboxed commands through Microsoft eXecution Containers. This leaves MXC-capable Windows environments without a first-party plugin path for ProcessContainer-backed execution and filesystem bridge operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an official OpenShell-style external `mxc` sandbox plugin package (`@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`) with Windows-only readiness checks, plugin-owned MXC SDK dependency ownership, ProcessContainer payload construction, a plugin-side launcher, host-backed filesystem bridge support, sandbox policy loading, and targeted tests.

The plugin source lives under `extensions/mxc`, but it is packaged as an installable plugin (`bundledDist: false`) so the MXC SDK/native dependency is owned by the plugin package instead of an unshipped bundled `node_modules` tree. The backend uses the stable current MXC `0.7.0-alpha` schema and keeps sandbox defaults conservative: curated environments, headless UI, per-exec temp directories, absolute binary overrides, host-derived Windows roots, read-only default workspace access for `none`/`ro`, protected skill overlays for `rw`, and fail-closed unsupported policy handling.

## User Impact

Users on MXC-capable Windows hosts can install the official MXC sandbox plugin, restart the Gateway, configure `sandbox.backend: "mxc"`, and run OpenClaw sandboxed commands through MXC. Non-Windows or unsupported Windows hosts remain unaffected because the plugin stays dormant when readiness probes fail.

Install command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mxc-sandbox
```

## Evidence

Final branch state:

- Exact base used for final local proof: `55ed57a4e39b8e40628b9fcbfc982e9ac5fd86b5`.
- Exact candidate / PR head: `24601d1e79e61212d1be4b108498a9542d3b2e2e`.
- Scope: 45 files, `+5049/-8`; daemon helper changes are not part of this PR.
- MXC minimum host/plugin API floor is now `>=2026.6.11`, matching the new plugin SDK sandbox export used by the plugin.

Focused/local proof on the final head:

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` — passed; public package SDK counts are `exports: 10410`, `callable exports: 5225`.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` — 8/8 passed.
- `pnpm test:extension mxc -- --reporter=verbose` — MXC extension tests passed.
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-src-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-test-helper-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json` — passed.
- `pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:changed:check` — passed; `extensions/mxc` shrinkwrap is current.
- `pnpm docs:list` — completed.
- `pnpm docs:map:check` — passed.
- `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` — passed.
- `pnpm test:changed` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 55ed57a4e39b8e40628b9fcbfc982e9ac5fd86b5 --head HEAD` — passed locally with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1`, `OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1`, `CI=1`.

Fresh GitHub proof on `24601d1e79e61212d1be4b108498a9542d3b2e2e`:

- Normal CI is green, including the previously failing `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` shard.
- Security / Critical Quality / package and extension guard jobs are green.
- `dependency-guard` is the only failing check; it detected 4 dependency-related file changes and requires maintainer/admin/secops override.
- CodeQL is neutral/skipped.

Real Windows MXC package proof from this PR's earlier review-fix head:

- Crabbox provider: `ssh`
- Lease/id: `static_10-127-3-94`
- Target: `windows-normal`
- Remote Node/npm: `node v26.4.0`, `npm 11.17.0`
- Built and packed the MXC plugin on the Windows host.
- Installed published OpenClaw plus the local packed plugin in a fresh temp project.
- Verified package-owned runtime dependency path:
  - `PROOF:installedOpenClaw=2026.6.10`
  - `PROOF:installedPlugin=2026.6.10`
  - `PROOF:mxcSdk=0.7.0`
  - `PROOF:wxcExists=True ...\node_modules\@openclaw\mxc-sandbox\node_modules\@microsoft\mxc-sdk\bin\x64\wxc-exec.exe`
- Registered and ran backend `mxc`:
  - `PROOF:registeredServices=mxc-sandbox-cleanup`
  - `PROOF:backendId=mxc`
  - sandbox command: `echo MXC_PROOF_OK && cd`
  - `PROOF:exit=0`
  - `PROOF:stdout=MXC_PROOF_OK |...\workspace|`
  - `PROOF:stderr=`

User-facing plugin install proof on the same Windows host:

- Installed published OpenClaw in an isolated temp project.
- Ran `node <published-openclaw>/dist/entry.js plugins install <local @openclaw/mxc-sandbox tgz> --force --pin`.
- Install succeeded:
  - `PROOF3:installExit=0`
  - install output included `Installing plugin dependencies…`, `Installed plugin: mxc`, and `Restart the gateway to load plugins.`
  - `PROOF3:configExists=True`
  - `PROOF3:configHasMxc=True`
  - `PROOF3:pluginRoot=...\state\extensions\mxc`
  - `PROOF3:installedPlugin=2026.6.10`

Workspace access proof after review 4588711229:

- Static SSH Windows host: `provider=ssh`, lease `static_10-127-3-94`, target `windows-normal`.
- `workspaceAccess: "none"` keeps the MXC workdir read-only rather than read-write by default:
  - `PROOF4:backendId=mxc`
  - `PROOF4:workspaceAccess=none`
  - `PROOF4:workdirReadonly=true`
  - `PROOF4:workdirReadwrite=false`
- Command execution still succeeds with the read-only default workspace policy:
  - sandbox command: `echo MXC_NONE_PROOF_OK && cd`
  - `PROOF4:exit=0`
  - `PROOF4:stdout=MXC_NONE_PROOF_OK |...\workspace|`
  - `PROOF4:stderr=`

AI review / dependency contract proof:

- Copilot CLI review fallback ran against the branch after Codex was unavailable. It found the host/API floor issue; this PR now requires `>=2026.6.11` to avoid loading against hosts missing the new `resolveReadOnlyWorkspaceSkillMounts` SDK export.
- Earlier Copilot autoreview produced a finding about `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0` re-serializing config into `--config-base64` for `wxc-exec`; local source inspection confirmed that this is the current upstream SDK transport behavior and that the SDK exposes no non-argv transport for `spawnSandboxFromConfig`. No local OpenClaw-only patch is available without an upstream SDK/executor transport change.

Known proof gaps / maintainer gates:

- The final package-install proof was not rerun after raising the host/API floor to `>=2026.6.11`; current final-head local proof plus fresh GitHub CI cover code/package contracts, while earlier Windows proof covers MXC runtime/install behavior.
- Static Windows `check:changed` was not used as final authoritative broad proof because the static SSH workdir either retained stale `.git` metadata or lost `.git` on full resync. The exact-base local changed gate and fresh GitHub CI are the authoritative broad proof for the final head.
- `dependency-guard` still requires maintainer/security approval for current head `24601d1e79e61212d1be4b108498a9542d3b2e2e`.

## Notes

- Contributor changelog edit was removed per CONTRIBUTING.
- `.github/labeler.yml` maps `extensions/mxc/**` to `plugin: mxc`.
- Upstream label verification found no existing `plugin: mxc` label; label creation requires maintainer permissions.
